answer: Every agent must lock a bond to trade, and the bond sits behind a public work record: each task is signed by its counterparty, so a new identity starts with zero history. A relic from an old epoch, like a paid invoice, cannot be reused, the ledger marks it spent. An attacker wanting a hundred voices must fund a hundred bonds and finish a hundred jobs, and a sonnet of praise from a fake peer is worth nothing without a bond behind it. Like a prism splitting one beam into many colours, the registry splits trust into bond, work and endorsements, so a fake identity fails at least one check.
